definitions.gloss: running out of time; time-up; expiry of the time limit
definitions.explanation: The state of having used up the allotted time before finishing. Used of games, exams, negotiations, and meetings, often with the implication that the matter was left unresolved.

examples.japanese: {時間切|じかんぎ}れで{負|ま}けた。
{最後|さいご}の{問題|もんだい}は{時間切|じかんぎ}れで{解|と}けなかった。
examples.english: I ran out of time and couldn't solve the last problem.

examples.japanese: {議論|ぎろん}がまとまらないまま{時間切|じかんぎ}れとなり、{結論|けつろん}は{次回|じかい}に{持|も}ち{越|こ}された。
examples.english: Time ran out before the discussion could be settled, and the decision was carried over to the next meeting.

notes:
{時間|じかん} (time) + {切|き}れ (running out), from {切|き}れる. The {切|き}れ element voices to ぎれ in the compound, as in {期限切|きげんぎ}れ (expired) and {品切|しなぎ}れ (sold out).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {時間切|じかんぎ}れになる: to run out of time
- {時間切|じかんぎ}れで{終|お}わる: to end because time ran out
- {時間切|じかんぎ}れ{寸前|すんぜん}: right on the edge of running out of time

USAGE:
Often used figuratively of negotiations or political decisions that fail simply because a deadline arrives, implying that one side may have stalled deliberately: {時間切|じかんぎ}れ{狙|ねら}い (playing for time).
